The jungler has zero tempo and loves to throw, leaving the mid laner to carry the whole game single-handedly. Playing like this against LCK feels completely hopeless. LCK loves farming these formulaic teams; as long as you make Knight uncomfortable, BLG just naturally collapses.

top.en: Bin has finally become what all the haters said he was, but BLG can never go back—they've completely turned into a second-rate team! Losing to MKOI isn't the scary part; the scary part is that Bin isn't carrying at all anymore. He's gone full Flandre, playing that 0 'non-stick pan' style, making his teammates comfortable while he waits to get carried. The cyberbullying after MSI was brutal. Everyone made Bin the scapegoat, flaming him and saying if he just played safe, BLG would win easily. They said, 'Just bring in a Flandre-type player who makes teammates comfortable, and they'll win the championship easily.' Well, how's it going now? Is it easy? The end result is losing to AL in the LPL finals—they can't even win the league! Xun played well at MSI, and ON was good too, but both of them are truly washed now, especially Xun—his performance in the third stage finals was inhuman. And Xun doesn't help Bin at all, focusing entirely on mid and bot. Many people see Bin getting out-CS'd now and think his laning has gotten worse, that he's not as good as before, not even able to crush a second-rate European top laner. But that's not the case at all! It's because BLG has stopped caring about Bin. They only want the bot lane to carry, or they focus on mid-jungle, leaving the top lane to fend for itself. The team's plan is for the top lane to just hold on and wait for teamfights. So, to stay stable, Bin's playstyle has shifted toward being cautious. He doesn't engage in aggressive trades with the opponent. If he trades too much, the enemy jungler might gank him, and since his own jungler won't help, he'd rather sacrifice CS, fall behind in gold, and even sacrifice himself in the draft by picking first and eating a counter-pick just to make his teammates comfortable. But now the teammates are comfortable, yet they aren't carrying. And as the sacrificial lamb, with no gold advantage and no tactical protection, how do you expect him to carry? Why was Bin so god-tier during the Herald season? Because the team built tactics around him! Because his laning was strong, he'd often crush his opponent, and Xun could just dive the tower to build him an advantage. Plus, they picked champions that protected his split-pushing—Pantheon, Shen—if anyone dared to gank Bin, he'd just fly away. Combined with Bin's elite individual skill, that's how BLG won the Herald season championship. But now, everything has changed. Sigh. I still miss the old, arrogant Bin. Too bad, we can never go back. I hope his sacrifices lead to a championship, otherwise, he should just leave.

top.en: Let me summarize for you: for the first 5 minutes, the jungler was always bot. Lee Sin hit a Q, but the W was dodged by Jarvan IV—you could say it was a good dodge. Then Xun hit a Q on Jarvan IV to chunk him and helped bot lane push the wave. At 5:40, Jarvan IV finished his Krugs and went home to buy items; Xun didn't go home and stayed in the bot river to camp. At 5:50, Nautilus hooked Ezreal, but the W missed; otherwise, Ezreal would have blown both summoners and the dragon would have been free. Then Xun went back to take the scuttle and the dragon. The dragon hit Nautilus twice, he called Xun for help, and he hooked Ezreal again, but the W still missed, so they couldn't take the dragon. Xun went home, and by this time Jarvan IV was out of mana. Note that Xun was basically playing with his cards on the table in the bot lane, and K'Sante in the top lane could have easily pushed the wave and taken tower plates. But Viper's mistakes meant that Xun and ON's two camping attempts resulted in nothing despite having the advantage. At 7:30, Nautilus lost his flash and was forced home, Ezreal pushed a wave and went home, then swapped to top for the Void Grubs, while Jhin stayed to eat another wave, causing him to arrive at the tier 2 tower just as Ezreal was leaving. Then Ezreal and K'Sante burned Bin's flash. Here, Bin saw an opportunity when K'Sante was about to recall and ulted Ezreal. At this point, if Viper had just hit his W, Ezreal would have been dead for sure, Camille would have gotten the kill, and they would have secured the Void Grubs to start snowballing. But he didn't. It doesn't matter, though—if Jhin had just ulted on the spot, Ezreal, still trapped in Camille's ult, would have had nowhere to run. But what was Viper doing? He walked for two seconds, stuttered his auto-attack, and just waited for Camille's ult to expire. Ezreal E'd away, and K'Sante came up to block, so he finally ulted, but it all hit K'Sante. There were at least three tempo points in the early game, each easier than the last. If he had just hit one W, they could have snowballed. Instead, they forced Xun to rush the dragon, and they only got some tempo after a gank under the tower with Knight. Later, they relied on others to carry in teamfights while he just coasted. I want to say, if they were playing against an LCK team, Xun wouldn't have found tempo that easily, and the bot lane would have been even worse. Then they'd continue to kidnap the jungler and sacrifice the top lane, leaving the top laner unable to fight back and forced to let the opponent farm. Even if you help, they can't carry; they'd still lose the 4v4, the top laner would have to TP, and the enemy top laner would get to farm beautifully. In the end, when the enemy top laner is styling on the ADC, are you going to ask who fed him? Isn't that something your bot lane fed themselves?
